newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-GIGGS AND CANTONA RESTORE MANCHESTER UNITED MORALE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIGGS AND CANTONA RESTORE MANCHESTER UNITED MORALE.

text.p: Ryan Giggs and Eric Cantona restored Manchester United's morale with the goals in a 2-0 win over Rapid Vienna which propelled the English side into the quarter-finals of the European Cup on Wednesday.
The victory gave United second place in Group C of the Champions' League and a quarter-final tie with Porto next March.

United's morale had been in tatters after two consecutive home defeats, their first at Old Trafford in 40 years of European competition, when they went down 1-0 to Juventus last month only three weeks after losing by the same score to Fenerbahce.
"I didn't think Juventus would let us down, or themselves," a delighted Manchester manager Alex Ferguson said.
Ryan Giggs opened the scoring for the English champions on a bitterly cold evening at Vienna's Ernst Happel stadium with a great shot in the 24th minute.
Giggs sent a cross from Roy Keane on to Eric Cantona, who threaded a beautiful pass through the Austrian defence for the Welsh forward to score.
In the second half, Cantona missed a gilt-edged chance in the 65th minute after a cross from Norway's Ole Gunnar Solskjaer when his header hit the post.
But the French striker made amends seven minutes later when he converted an excellent cross from David Beckham to make it 2-0.

"I think we deserved to win. I am satisfied with the way the team played. At times we played good football and at times we showed composure," said Ferguson. "There was a five minute period when Rapid were so strong we were almost punished.

United set the pace from the start with Giggs missing a clear chance when he blazed over the bar in the sixth minute. Four minutes later Gary Neville hit a thunderbolt shot which Rapid goalkeeper Michael Konsel did well to tip over the post.
But Rapid -- who have not played competitively for the past fortnight as the Austrian league has begun its winter break -- gave the English club a fright.
Forward Rene Wagner forced Manchester's Danish goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel to a great save in the 15th minute when he dived low to his right and somehow scooped the ball over the bar.
"Schmeichel's save was absolutely fantastic," commented Ferguson.
Play became rougher towards the end and United had Keane and Nicky Butt carried off injured in the 76th and 78th minutes respectively.
"Keane has a bad gash below his knee which will keep him out of action until the New Year," said Ferguson.
Ernst Dokupil, coach of the Austrian first division leaders, said: "There were a lot of opportunities on both sides. We failed to make use of our chances."
It was Rapid's first home defeat in 13 European matches.

Rapid Vienna: 1-Michael Konsel, 4-Trifon Ivanov, 5-Peter Schoettel, 19-Thomas Zingler, 11-Christian Prosenik, 20-Andreas Heraf, 10-Didi Kuehbauer, 6-Peter Stoeger (18-Sergej Mandreko 66), 16-Krzysztof Ratajczyk, 17-Rene Wagner, 7-Christian Stumpf (9-Marek Penksa 63)
